newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index starts bourse at record high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index starts bourse at record high.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares started bourse dealings at a record high on Monday, continuing the rally started last week, with the market supported by a firmer dollar and strength on Wall Street.
The DAX index hit a new bourse record of 2,860.24 points in early trade, before paring gains slightly to stand up 9.49 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,855.01 points.
But dealers said volumes were thin and said the market was not likely to be able to keep up the tempo set last week, when the DAX gained three percent.

Analysts had not been expecting the 2,850 point level to be breached until the end of the year, but the DAX has rallied strongly in the last week, boosted in particular by dollar strength, benefiting German exporters.
The dollar climbed above the crucial 1.54 mark level on Monday, reaching its highest point for almost six weeks.
The chemical sector was particularly encouraged by dollar strength, BASF AG, Bayer AG and Hoechst AG shares all rising strongly.

Meanwhile, shares in Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank fell 45 pfennigs to 72.85 marks after a newspaper reported its asset management unit Morgan Grenfell would have to repatriate 200 million sterling.
Deutsche Bank called the 200 million sterling figure "speculation", but admitted it would have to pay an unspecified level of compensation to investors.

Dealers said the legal dispute between carmaker Volkswagen and U.S. giant General Motors would continue to keep VW shares under pressure. VW shares fell almost four percent, or 23.50 marks, to 593 marks.

Shares in chemicals and metals group Degussa AG climbed nine marks to 647 marks after the company said pretax profits for the 1995/96 financial year rose two percent and said it expected business to continue well.
